definitions.explanation: A condition that must be met or a qualification that is necessary. Commonly used in legal, business, and technical contexts.

definitions.gloss: matter of business, purpose of a visit or call
definitions.explanation: The reason or business purpose for contacting or visiting someone. A polite way to ask what someone needs.

examples.japanese: {応募|おうぼ}{要件|ようけん}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
{法律|ほうりつ}の{要件|ようけん}を{満|み}たしていない。
examples.english: It does not meet the legal requirements.

examples.japanese: システムの{要件|ようけん}{定義|ていぎ}を{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: We will carry out the system requirements definition.

examples.japanese: ご{要件|ようけん}は{何|なん}でしょうか。
examples.english: What is your business? / How can I help you?

examples.japanese: {要件|ようけん}だけ{伝|つた}えて{電話|でんわ}を{切|き}った。
examples.english: I conveyed just the business matter and hung up.

examples.japanese: {急|いそ}ぎの{要件|ようけん}があるので、{手短|てみじか}にお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: I have an urgent matter, so please keep it brief.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 ({要件|ようけん} as requirement) is common in formal, legal, and technical writing. In IT, {要件|ようけん}{定義|ていぎ} (requirements definition) is a standard project phase. Sense 2 ({要件|ようけん} as business matter) is polite and often heard in business phone calls and office settings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {要件|ようけん}を{満|み}たす: to meet requirements
- {要件|ようけん}{定義|ていぎ}: requirements definition
- {応募|おうぼ}{要件|ようけん}: application requirements
- ご{要件|ようけん}は: what is your business (polite)
- {必須|ひっす}{要件|ようけん}: mandatory requirement

SIMILAR WORDS:
{用件|ようけん} (business, errand) is a homophone written with different kanji. {用件|ようけん} is exclusively sense 2 — the purpose of a call or visit. {条件|じょうけん} (condition, terms) is broader and less formal than {要件|ようけん} in the "requirement" sense.
